newsitem.title: UK: NWE low sulphur straight-run fuel offered higher.
newsitem.headline: NWE low sulphur straight-run fuel offered higher.

text.p: European low sulphur straight-run was offered a little higher on Friday but buyers were waiting for other sellers to show their material to drive down prices, traders said.
One seller was said offering its early to mid July material at more than $100 a tonne fob to two potential buyers.
Traders said one offer for 50,000 tonnes of low sulphur straight-run loading July 10-15 was made to a U.S.-based indepedent refiner at three figures.
But the refiner was said to be waiting until other sellers come into the market "to play them off against each other", a trader said.
"At first glance it seems we have a higher number today," the trader added.
Low sulphur straight run last traded at $99 fob earlier this week and the buyer of that cargo, a U.K.-based major, said it would be waiting for other sellers to come out to get a better deal.
Some traders said low sulphur straight-run would also be under pressure next week from falling crude prices.
